newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran military plane crash kills more than 80.
newsitem.headline: Iran military plane crash kills more than 80.

text.p: An Iranian military plane with about 8O people on board crashed in a mountainous region in northeastern Iran, killing all passengers and crew, the official news agency IRNA said on Friday.
It quoted an aviation official as saying 78 of those aboard the C-130 Hercules transport plane which crashed on Thursday were military men and the remaining were family members.
State-run Tehran radio earlier said there were 86 on board the plane which was flying to the city of Mashhad from the soutwestern city of Dezful.
The plane disappeared in mountains near Neyshabour, 75 km (47 miles) west of Mashhad after the pilot reported engine failure.
IRNA said the the plane crashed at 6 p.m. (1430 GMT) on Thursday.

The victims included eight members of the Revolutionary Guards, 48 army and army aviation personnel and 22 staff members of Iran's military logistics headquarters, IRNA said. It did not give their ranks.
The accident is the latest in a series of air crashes in the past few years involving civilian and military planes, most of which date from before the 1979 Islamic revolution.
Iranian authorities have blamed some of the accidents on technical failures in the ageing planes but have not fully explained the causes of other crashes.
Earlier this month, four Iranians were killed when a light military transport plane on a relief mission to Iran's quake-stricken northwest crashed in bad weather.
In April 1995, a military training plane crashed south of Tehran during an armed forces day parade, killing the pilot and injuring four people when the wreckage hit residential areas.

In January 1995, an airforce Lockheed C-140 JetStar A plane crash killed Iran's air force commander along with four generals and seven other officers. The incident was the second time since the revolution that the country's air force chief and senior officers had died in a plane crash.
In October 1994, a Fokker F-28 of the state-owned Asseman airlines with 66 people on board, crashed on a flight from Isfahan to Tehran. There were no survivors.

In March 1994, a military C-130 plane, bringing home families of Iranian diplomats in Moscow, was hit by a missile apparently fired by Armenian forces in the disputed Nagorno-Karabakh region in Azerbaijan. All 32 people on board were killed.
In February 1993, a Sukhoi fighter crashed in mid-air near Tehran with a Tupolev Tu-154 chartered by a subsidiary of the state carrier Iran Air. All 134 people aboard the two planes were killed.
